hunt.justification: The shift toward consent loopholes and the weaponization of trusted first-party applications allows adversaries to maintain long-term persistent access that survives MFA and password resets. Identifying this abuse requires correlating identity logs with cloud API activity, which a negative result over the estate confirms is not actively occurring.

This hunt uses the baseline of rare app consents to find the needle in the haystack across three identity and cloud telemetry surfaces.

scenario.summary: Adversaries are weaponizing trust across the enterprise stack by abusing legitimate tools like ScreenConnect, AI coding assistants, and Microsoft first-party clients. Intrusions leverage AiTM phishing to bypass MFA and deploy signed payloads via DLL sideloading, often achieving full compromise from infection to cloud login in just eight minutes.

meta.rationale: Prioritize users with privileged roles (hb_users privileged = true) or those who have signed in from unusual geographic locations recently. Focus the parallel queries by pasting usernames with proxy sign-ins into the scope_users list.
meta.hypothesis: An adversary has bypassed MFA by stealing a session cookie via AiTM phishing or an infostealer, then logged into a cloud tenant and granted permissions to a malicious or rare application to ensure persistent access.

hunt.name: SaaS Identity and Consent Loophole Abuse
hunt.description: This hunt examines the identity and cloud control plane for signs of the consent loophole and AiTM phishing observed in the Nov 2026 report. It identifies successful logins originating from anonymizing proxies or carrying high-risk states, then corroborates these by looking for rare OAuth application consent events associated with those same users. The hunt focuses on the critical 8-minute window where session theft transitions to persistent cloud access through first-party app abuse.

nodes.label: Suspect sign-ins from proxies or high-risk states

config.content: SELECT time, actor_user_name, src_endpoint_ip, src_location_country, client_app, risk_state, is_proxy, auth_requirement, device_trust_type FROM hb_auth_signin WHERE status_id = 1 AND (risk_state IN ('atRisk', 'confirmedCompromised') OR is_proxy = 'true') AND ('{{scope_users}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_users}}' || ',', ',' || actor_user_name || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
config.description: Identify successful logins that are marked at risk or originate from anonymizing proxies, which are common indicators of AiTM phishing kits.
config.expected_signal: Rows indicating successful logins despite high risk states or proxy origin. Silence indicates no obvious AiTM-style session usage was detected by the provider's risk engine.

nodes.label: Detail session attributes for the suspect users

config.content: SELECT time, actor_user_name, src_endpoint_ip, src_location_country, user_agent, client_app, auth_protocol, auth_requirement, device_trust_type, status_detail FROM hb_auth_signin WHERE status_id = 1 AND ('{{scope_users}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_users}}' || ',', ',' || actor_user_name || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
config.description: Collect detailed attributes for the sign-ins of the users identified in the lead, focusing on device trust and user agents.
config.expected_signal: A history of sign-ins for the target users, allowing for comparison of location and device trust between normal and suspicious logins.

config.content: SELECT resource_name AS app_name, api_operation, COUNT(DISTINCT actor_user_name) AS distinct_users, MIN(time) AS first_consent_time, MAX(time) AS last_consent_time FROM hb_cloud_api_activity WHERE (LOWER(api_operation) LIKE '%consent%' OR LOWER(api_operation) LIKE '%add app role assignment%' OR LOWER(api_operation) LIKE '%update application%') AND provider IN ('azure_ad', 'm365') AND ('{{scope_users}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_users}}' || ',', ',' || actor_user_name || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY resource_name, api_operation HAVING distinct_users <= 5
config.description: Identify OAuth application consents or app role assignments for the targeted users that are rare across the fleet, highlighting potential malicious apps used for the consent loophole.
config.expected_signal: Applications that have been granted consent by only a few users, specifically those in our scope. If a user from the lead query is in this list, it strongly suggests identity abuse.

config.objective: Evaluate whether any user has a successful proxy sign-in followed by a rare application consent or role assignment, paying specific attention to the timestamp correlation.
config.description: The agent determines whether the sign-ins and rare app consents constitute a session theft and persistence attempt.
config.expected_signal: A per-user verdict indicating whether the proxy login was followed by a rare application consent within the reported 8-minute window.
config.success_criteria: A verdict of malicious | suspicious | benign per user, citing specific login and API rows.

Stop active adversary access by revoking all refresh tokens and active sessions for the compromised account.
config.instructions: Revoke all refresh tokens and sessions for the users identified as malicious. Review and remove any recently consented applications in the tenant.

nodes.label: Verify remediation and check for persistence

config.description: Ensure the adversary has no other persistence mechanisms like new administrative accounts or hidden enterprise applications.
config.instructions: Manually verify the removal of malicious app registrations. Check for any new administrative roles assigned during the compromise window. Review hb_account_change for password resets.
